In a program compiled with [`bun build --compile --aot`](/bundler/executables#ahead-of-time-compilation), the objects that JavaScript itself provides are immutable. The compiler relies on `Array.prototype.push` and `Math.max` being what they are. A write that works without `--aot` throws a `TypeError` there. Most such writes run while a module loads, so the program doesn't start.

| What                                | Such as                                       | Under `--aot`                             |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| A built-in prototype                | `Array.prototype`, `Object.prototype`         | keeps its properties, and gets no new ones |
| Any other built-in object           | `Date`, `Math`, `JSON`, `Intl.DateTimeFormat` | keeps its properties, and can get new ones unless they hide an inherited one |
| The global variables that name them | `Date`, `Promise`, `parseInt`                 | can't be replaced or deleted              |

What Bun adds to JavaScript stays mutable: `console`, `process`, `setTimeout`, `fetch`, `URL`, `Buffer` and so on.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/aot-locked-builtin-write" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
Array.prototype.last = function () {
  return this[this.length - 1];
};
```

{/* bad {"count": 4} */}
```js
Date.now = () => 0;
delete JSON.parse;
globalThis.Date = FakeDate;
Array.prototype.__proto__ = {};
```

The functions of `Object` that change an object throw too:

{/* bad {"count": 4} */}
```js
Object.defineProperty(Object.prototype, "should", { get: makeAssertion });
Object.defineProperties(String.prototype, { shout: { value: shout } });
Object.assign(Math, { random: () => 0.5 });
Object.setPrototypeOf(Date, {});
```

Those of `Reflect` return `false` and change nothing:

{/* bad */}
```js
const isReplaced = Reflect.set(Math, "random", () => 0.5);
```

A cast or another name for the prototype makes no difference:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```ts
(String.prototype as any).shout = function () {
  return this.toUpperCase() + "!";
};

const proto = Array.prototype;
Object.defineProperty(proto, "last", { get: lastOf });
```

A new property can't hide one that the object inherits from another built-in object. Here that is `Function.prototype.toString`:

{/* bad */}
```js
Date.toString = () => "today";
```

Not reported:

Write a function that takes the value, or a subclass.

{/* good */}
```js
function last(list) {
  return list[list.length - 1];
}

class List extends Array {
  last() {
    return this[this.length - 1];
  }
}
```

A constructor or a namespace can get a new property. Only prototypes can't.

{/* good */}
```js
Math.clamp = (n, low, high) => Math.min(Math.max(n, low), high);
```

What Bun adds to JavaScript, and the two settings of `Error`:

{/* good */}
```js
console.log = () => {};
globalThis.fetch = async () => new Response("ok");
Error.stackTraceLimit = 50;
Error.prepareStackTrace = (error, frames) => frames.join("\n");
```

A polyfill guarded by a test for a feature that Bun already has. The write never runs:

{/* good */}
```js
if (!Array.prototype.flat) {
  Array.prototype.flat = flat;
}
if (typeof Object.assign !== "function") {
  Object.defineProperty(Object, "assign", { value: assign });
}
Object.hasOwn ||= hasOwn;
Number.isNaN = Number.isNaN || isNaN;
```

Something else of the same name:

{/* good */}
```js
import { Date } from "./fake-date";

Date.now = () => 0;
```

What JavaScript itself refuses, with or without `--aot`:

{/* good */}
```js
Math.PI = 3;
Array.prototype = {};
```

## What it doesn't find

The rule looks at one file, and only at writes in which the object is written out. It doesn't find `target[name] = value` where `target` turns out to be `globalThis`, a destructuring assignment such as `[Date.now] = [fake]`, or a write in a package that you don't lint. [`bun --aot-audit`](/bundler/aot-adoption) finds those while your program runs: it logs a `would-refuse` line for each.

## Related rules

[`no-extend-native`](/lint/rules/eslint/no-extend-native) reports `Array.prototype.last = ..` and `Object.defineProperty(Array.prototype, ..)`, and [`no-global-assign`](/lint/rules/eslint/no-global-assign) reports `Date = ..`. Where one of them is on and reports a place, this rule doesn't report it again.
